scientific_scope_status: For finite N>=2, supplied complex y,z and real symmetric nearest-neighbour H, nonzero s_j=Im(conj(y_j)*y_(j+1)) and Im<y,z>=0 determine a unique H satisfying Hy=z. Its hoppings are J_j=sum_(k<=j)Im(conj(y_k)*z_k)/s_j; the real diagonal follows row by row. This compiles one vector response at one design energy. It does not ensure a common response for several inputs, positive signal energy, a stable bath completion, uniform bandwidth or a physical gate. The source also reports failed five-mode dynamics and improved reciprocal/local numerical trials, whose governing files were not supplied.

validation.internal: Completed source-exposed intake-author reconstruction of the finite real-Jacobi response theorem from native lines48–66. Taking imaginary row products gives t_j=-J_(j-1)*s_(j-1)+J_j*s_j; prefix summation fixes every hopping and the global sum enforces the last row. The explicit real diagonal then closes Hy=z and gives uniqueness. Exact Gaussian-rational small-chain recovery, incompatible global/zero-current cases, a simultaneous-response counterexample and an ill-conditioned nonpositive family check these boundaries. The last two are curator algebraic diagnostics, not producer photonic ports or a broad device no-go. No original scientific program, numerical scattering/Schur/TE-grid suite, Maxwell solver, primary-paper audit or physical experiment was executed. Numerical claims remain source reports, and one-body positivity is not a many-body/continuum gap or complete operation.
